question: What are common algorithms implemented in Collections Framework?
answerMd:
### Comprehensive Analysis of the Java Collections Framework (JCF)

#### 1. Architectural Blueprint:
```
                         java.lang.Iterable<T>
                                  |
                        java.util.Collection<E>
                                  |
         +------------------------+------------------------+
         |                                                 |
      List<E>                                           Set<E>
  (Indexed, Duplicates)                          (Unique elements)
         |                                                 |
  +------+------+                                   +------+------+
  |             |                                   |             |
ArrayList   LinkedList                           HashSet       TreeSet
Vector                                         LinkedHashSet (SortedSet)

                      java.util.Map<K, V> (Independent Hierarchy)
                                  |
              +-------------------+-------------------+
              |                                       |
           HashMap                                 TreeMap
        LinkedHashMap                            (NavigableMap)
```

#### 2. Detailed Technical Comparison of Core Interfaces:
| Interface | Element Ordering | Duplicates Allowed | Null Values | Best Implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`List`** | Preserves insertion order (indexed $0 \dots n-1$). | **Yes** | Yes (multiple) | `ArrayList` (fast access), `LinkedList` (fast insertion). |
| **`Set`** | No guarantee (except `TreeSet` sorted). | **No** (strictly unique) | `HashSet` allows 1 null; `TreeSet` allows 0 nulls. | `HashSet` ($O(1)$ lookup), `TreeSet` ($O(\log n)$ sorted). |
| **`Queue`** | FIFO (First-In, First-Out) or Priority. | **Yes** | No | `ArrayDeque` (double-ended), `PriorityQueue`. |
| **`Map`** | Keys: Unordered (except `TreeMap` sorted). | Keys: **No**; Values: **Yes** | `HashMap` allows 1 null key; `TreeMap` 0 null keys. | `HashMap` ($O(1)$ key lookup), `TreeMap` (sorted keys). |

$$\therefore \text{The Java Collections Framework optimizes memory and execution efficiency for data structures.}$$
